text.p: WasteMasters Inc said Friday it had removed Richard Masters as its president, chief executive and member of the executive committee effective July 14.
Peter Stefanou, acting chief financial officer, will now also act as interim president and chief executive, it said.
It also said in a statement that it was negotiating the potential sale of "certain" landfill assets to a wholly-owned subsidiary of Continental Investment Corp.

The company said in a statement that it had to obtain approval from the board of directors and a majority of the shareholders before it could sell "substantially all" of its assets to Continental Technologies Corp.
The company did not elaborate on how much of its assets it planned to sell and officials at both WasteMasters and Continental were not available for comment.
In addition, WasteMasters said the board ratified an agreement with private investment group WMI Investors Inc for a $1 million credit line to meet working capital needs.

The loan agreement grants WMI a warrant to purchase 49 percent of the company's outstanding common stock and 100,000 shares of preferred stock, it said. WasteMasters said it expected to close the deal within the next 10 days.
In May, the company received $300,000 from a private placement to meet immediate working capital requirements. It had also retained Star Funding Inc to obtain $6 million of long-term debt financing.
